title: Multi-LoRA serving
brief: Write the LoRA update, then serve many adapters in one batch with a gathered bgmv and a segmented sgmv. Count the adapter bytes and PCIe loads, and keep adapters resident with an eviction policy graded on a seeded trace.
hints: The update is x W + (x A) B times alpha / r. The scale is alpha divided by the rank, and the rank is A.shape[1].
bgmv gathers A_stack[adapter_ids] and B_stack[adapter_ids], so the gather index is the request's adapter id, not its position in the batch. An id of -1 means the base layer only.
sgmv sorts the rows with a stable argsort, runs one pair of matmuls per segment, and writes the result back with out[order] = sorted_out.
A rank-r adapter on a (d_in, d_out) layer holds r * (d_in + d_out) values. The MLP adapter covers gate, up, and down in all 64 layers, at 2 bytes per value.
Every adapter in the current batch is pinned. Choose a victim from the other resident adapters: FIFO by load order, LRU by last step used, freq by lifetime batch count then LRU.
Count the use of every adapter in the batch before any load, so the frequency counts do not depend on the order inside a batch.
